node_rer_ser.title: Rough & Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER / SER)
node_rer_ser.subtitle: Continuous Interconnected Membrane Tubules & Sheets | Calcium Sequestration

metrics.membrane_continuity: Continuous with the outer nuclear envelope membrane
metrics.ser_functions: Lipid/sterol synthesis, phospholipid biosynthesis, and intracellular Ca2+ storage
metrics.calcium_pump: SERCA pump (Sarco/Endoplasmic Reticulum Ca2+-ATPase) maintaining ~1 mM lumen Ca2+

mechanism: The Endoplasmic Reticulum forms a vast continuous network of flattened sheets (Rough ER, densely studded with translating ribosomes for secretory and membrane protein synthesis) and tubular structures (Smooth ER, specialized for lipid metabolism and drug detoxification).

The ER lumen acts as the primary intracellular calcium (Ca2+) store. High-affinity binding proteins like Calreticulin and Calsequestrin bind free Ca2+, which can be rapidly released into the cytosol via IP3 receptor channels or Ryanodine receptors to trigger signaling cascades.
csir_high_yield: Marker Enzyme Alert (CSIR Part B): Glucose-6-Phosphatase (which hydrolyzes G6P to Glucose in the final step of gluconeogenesis) is localized exclusively to the Endoplasmic Reticulum membrane.

Membrane Biogenesis: Phospholipids are synthesized on the cytosolic leaflet of the SER membrane; Scramblases randomly flip them to the luminal leaflet to maintain symmetric bilayer growth before vesicular budding to the Golgi.
pathology: Darier Disease: Autosomal dominant mutations in ATP2A2 (encoding the SERCA2 calcium pump) disrupt ER calcium homeostasis, causing abnormal epidermal cell adhesion and keratotic skin lesions.
lab_workbench: Fluorescence Resonance Energy Transfer (FRET) using genetically encoded targeted cameleon Ca2+ indicators (ER-cameleon) allows real-time microscopic measurement of luminal ER calcium concentrations.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (3W5A — Crystal Structure of Mammalian SERCA1a Calcium Pump)

node_golgi_stack.title: The Golgi Apparatus (Cis, Medial & Trans Cisternae)
node_golgi_stack.subtitle: Polarized Glycosylation & Vesicular Sorting Station

metrics.polarity: Cis-Golgi Network (CGN) facing ER -> Medial Cisternae -> Trans-Golgi Network (TGN) facing Plasma Membrane

mechanism: Proteins and lipids synthesized in the ER arrive at the cis-Golgi network via COPII vesicular carriers. As they progress through the polarized cisternae via cisternal maturation, they undergo sequential post-translational modifications.

Cis-Golgi adds Mannose-6-Phosphate (M6P) tags to acid hydrolases; medial cisternae trim mannoses and add GlcNAc; trans-Golgi and TGN perform sulfation, sialylation, and final sorting into clathrin-coated vesicles destined for lysosomes, secretory granules, or the plasma membrane.
csir_high_yield: Marker Enzymes for Fractionation (CSIR Favorite): Mannosidase II is the classic marker for medial Golgi cisternae; Galactosyltransferase marks trans-Golgi cisternae; Sialyltransferase marks the TGN.

O-linked glycosylation occurs exclusively in the Golgi (on Serine/Threonine hydroxyl groups), whereas N-linked glycosylation begins in the RER (on Asparagine side chains) and is modified in the Golgi.
pathology: I-Cell Disease (Mucolipidosis II): Deficiency of N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphotransferase in the cis-Golgi prevents the addition of Mannose-6-Phosphate tags to lysosomal enzymes. Without M6P, enzymes are secreted constitutively into the blood, leaving lysosomes engorged with undigested substrates (inclusion bodies).
lab_workbench: Pulse-Chase Radiosulfur (35S-Met/Cys) Labeling combined with Endo H (Endoglycosidase H) digestion: Endo H cleaves high-mannose N-linked glycans added in the ER, but is resistant to complex glycans modified in the medial/trans Golgi, tracking transit kinetics.

node_free_polysomes.title: Cytosolic Free Polysomes
node_free_polysomes.subtitle: Translational Machinery for Nuclear, Cytosolic & Mitochondrial Proteins

metrics.ribosome_pool: Identical 80S ribosomes shared freely between cytosolic and RER pools
metrics.destinations: Nucleoplasm, Cytosol, Peroxisomes, and Mitochondrial Matrix (via TOM/TIM complexes)
metrics.aggregation: Multiple ribosomes translating a single mRNA simultaneously (Polysome)

mechanism: Free polysomes float unattached in the cytoplasm and synthesize proteins that remain in the cytosol (e.g., glycolytic enzymes), fold into the nucleus (histones, transcription factors), or import post-translationally into peroxisomes and mitochondria.

There is no intrinsic structural difference between a ribosome translating on free polysomes and one bound to the rough ER; the destination of the protein is determined entirely by the presence or absence of an N-terminal signal peptide recognized co-translationally by SRP.
csir_high_yield: Post-Translational vs. Co-Translational Import: Proteins destined for mitochondria, chloroplasts, peroxisomes, and the nucleus are synthesized on free polysomes and imported POST-translationally (kept unfolded by cytosolic Hsp70 chaperones). Proteins destined for the ER, Golgi, lysosomes, or plasma membrane are imported CO-translationally.

Polysome profiles separated on sucrose density gradients show distinct peaks for monosomes (80S), disomes, and heavy polysomes; EDTA treatment chelates Mg2+ and dissociates polysomes back into 40S and 60S subunits.
pathology: Mitochondrial Import Defect Syndromes: Mutations in mitochondrial presequence translocases (e.g., TIMM8a) block post-translational import of cytosolic precursors into mitochondria, causing Mohr-Tranebjærg syndrome (deafness-dystonia).
lab_workbench: Polysome Profiling (Sucrose Gradient Centrifugation coupled with continuous 254 nm UV absorbance monitoring): Evaluates global translation initiation efficiency and ribosome stalling in response to stress or drugs.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (6EK0 — Cryo-EM Structure of the Mammalian Mitochondrial Ribosome 55S)

metrics.srp_composition: 7SL RNA + 6 distinct protein subunits (SRP54 binds the signal peptide via a M-domain)
metrics.srp_receptor: Heterodimer of SRα and SRβ anchored to the ER membrane
metrics.gtp_requirement: Both SRP54 and SRα bind GTP; mutual GTP hydrolysis opens the translocon seal

mechanism: STEP 1 (Signal Recognition): As a hydrophobic N-terminal Signal Peptide (~6–15 hydrophobic amino acids) emerges from the ribosomal exit tunnel, the 54 kDa subunit of the Signal Recognition Particle (SRP) binds it with high affinity, causing an immediate pause in translation elongation.
STEP 2 (Membrane Docking): The SRP-ribosome-nascent chain complex docks onto the ER membrane by binding the SRP Receptor (SR).

STEP 3 (Hand-Off): Both SRP54 and the SRalpha subunit bind GTP. Interaction between the two GTPases stimulates mutual GTP hydrolysis (GTP -> GDP + Pi), releasing SRP back to the cytoplasm and transferring the ribosome directly to the Sec61 translocon channel.
csir_high_yield: Classic CSIR NET Trap: SRP is a RIBONUCLEOPROTEIN complex containing 7SL RNA (which acts as a structural scaffold holding the protein subunits together). The RNA itself does not catalyze peptide bonds here, unlike rRNA in the ribosome.

Translational Pausing: Binding of SRP to the signal peptide induces a transient elongation arrest, preventing the full-length protein from being released into the cytosol before its ER destination is secured.
pathology: Autoantibodies against SRP occur in severe autoimmune myopathies (immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy), causing profound muscle weakness and regeneration failure.
lab_workbench: In Vitro Translation-Translocation Assay: Dog pancreas microsomal membranes added to rabbit reticulocyte lysate cell-free translation of secretory proteins demonstrate co-translational translocation (evidenced by N-linked glycosylation molecular weight shifts).

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (1RY1 — Crystal Structure of the SRP54 M-Domain Bound to Signal Peptide)

node_sec61_translocon.title: The Sec61 Translocon Complex
node_sec61_translocon.subtitle: Hourglass Aqueous Channel with a Luminal Plug and Lateral Gate

metrics.subunit_structure: Heterotrimer of Sec61α, β, and γ (Forms a dynamic aqueous pore)
metrics.sealing_mechanisms: A luminal alpha-helical 'Plug' (blocks ion leaks) and a Hydrophobic 'Lateral Gate'
metrics.transmembrane_insertion: Hydrophobic stop-transfer anchors slide out laterally into the lipid bilayer

mechanism: The Sec61 complex forms an hourglass-shaped aqueous channel across the ER membrane. When idle, a small alpha-helical 'plug' domain blocks the extracellular/luminal opening to prevent passive leakage of calcium and small metabolites.

When a translating ribosome docks, the incoming signal peptide inserts into the central pore, displacing the plug and opening the channel. Concurrently, the hydrophobic 'lateral gate' (facing the lipid bilayer) opens up, allowing hydrophobic transmembrane domains to partition directly out of the aqueous channel and slide sideways into the ER phospholipid bilayer.
csir_high_yield: Type I vs. Type II Membrane Protein Orientation (Guaranteed CSIR Part C Question):

• Type I Proteins (N-terminus in lumen, C-terminus in cytosol): Possess an N-terminal cleavable signal sequence (cleaved by Signal Peptidase) followed by a hydrophobic stop-transfer anchor sequence that halts translocation.

• Type II Proteins (N-terminus in cytosol, C-terminus in lumen): Lack a cleavable signal sequence; instead, they possess a single internal uncleaved 'signal-anchor sequence' whose positive flanking charges dictate orientation (positive-inside rule).
pathology: Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Liver Disease (ADPLD): Mutations in SEC61B (encoding Sec61 beta subunit) impair transmembrane glycoprotein biogenesis, leading to hepatic cyst formation.
lab_workbench: Photoaffinity Labeling with Benzophenone-modified Signal Peptides: Cross-links the nascent signal peptide directly to the Sec61alpha transmembrane segments (specifically helices 2 and 7) to map translocon architecture.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (3JC2 — Cryo-EM Structure of the Mammalian Ribosome-Sec61 Translocon Complex)

metrics.large_subunit_rnas: 28S rRNA (Peptidyl transferase ribozyme), 5.8S rRNA, and 5S rRNA

mechanism: SMALL 40S SUBUNIT: Binds the 5' m7G cap of mRNA via eIF4F (eIF4E + eIF4G + eIF4A helicase) and scans 5'->3' until it encounters the first Kozak consensus start site (5'-ACCAUGG-3') carrying Met-tRNAiMet.
LARGE 60S SUBUNIT: Joins upon hydrolysis of GTP by eIF5B, locking the 80S initiation complex together with the initiator tRNA positioned in the P-site, ready for elongation.
csir_high_yield: Prokaryotic (70S) vs. Eukaryotic (80S) Ribosome Contrast (CSIR Staple):

• Prokaryotic 70S = 30S small subunit (16S rRNA) + 50S large subunit (23S + 5S rRNAs). Target of Aminoglycosides (Streptomycin binds 16S), Tetracyclines, Chloramphenicol, and Macrolides (Erythromycin binds 23S).
• Eukaryotic 80S = 40S small subunit (18S rRNA) + 60S large subunit (28S + 5.8S + 5S rRNAs). Target of Cycloheximide, Ricin, and Alpha-sarcin.

Shine-Dalgarno vs. Kozak: Bacteria use the Shine-Dalgarno sequence (AGGAGG) base-pairing with 16S rRNA to position the start codon; Eukaryotes use 5' m7G cap-dependent scanning (Kozak rule: GCCRCCATGG).
pathology: Ricin Toxin from castor beans: An N-glycosidase that depurinates a specific Adenine residue (A4324) in the 28S rRNA loop of the 60S subunit, permanently inactivating elongation factor binding and halting all protein synthesis.
lab_workbench: Ribosome Profiling (Ribo-Seq): Treating cell lysates with RNase digests unprotected free mRNA, leaving only ribosome-protected fragments (~30 nt) that are deep-sequenced to map exact in vivo translation efficiency at codon resolution.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (4V6X — Cryo-EM Structure of the Mammalian 80S Ribosome)

node_a_p_e_sites.title: The A, P, and E Functional tRNA Binding Sites
node_a_p_e_sites.subtitle: Aminoacyl, Peptidyl, and Exit Sites on the Ribosomal Inter-Subunit Bridge

metrics.a_site: Aminoacyl site (Binds incoming aminoacyl-tRNA delivered by eEF1A-GTP)
metrics.p_site: Peptidyl site (Holds tRNA carrying the growing polypeptide chain)
metrics.e_site: Exit site (Holds deacylated tRNA before dissociation into cytosol)

mechanism: During each elongation cycle, tRNAs progress sequentially through three distinct sites spanning both the 40S decoding center and 60S catalytic core:
1. A-SITE: Incoming aminoacyl-tRNA binds here, tested for correct codon-anticodon complementarity (facilitated by 18S rRNA base-pairing checkpoints).
2. P-SITE: Holds the peptidyl-tRNA whose ester bond is attacked by the amino group of the aminoacyl-tRNA in the A-site.
3. E-SITE: After peptide bond formation, the deacylated tRNA shifts into the E-site (Exit) and rapidly dissociates from the ribosome.
csir_high_yield: Exception to the P-site Rule: The initiator Methionyl-tRNA (Met-tRNAiMet) is the ONLY aminoacyl-tRNA that binds DIRECTLY into the P-site without visiting the A-site first! All subsequent elongator aminoacyl-tRNAs must enter via the A-site.

Puromycin Antibiotic Trap (Classic CSIR Part C Question): Puromycin is a structural analog of the 3' terminal adenosine of aminoacyl-tRNA. It enters the ribosomal A-site, accepts the nascent polypeptide chain from the P-site via peptidyl transferase, forms a peptidyl-puromycin adduct, and prematurely dissociates from the ribosome, causing immediate chain termination!
pathology: Shiga Toxin & Diphtheria Toxin: Inhibit protein synthesis by modifying elongation factors (Diphtheria toxin ADP-ribosylates Diphtamide on eEF2, halting translocation).
lab_workbench: In Vitro Amino Acid Incorporation Assay: Incubating purified ribosomes with 14C-labeled amino acids, tRNA, and GTP to measure total synthetic output in the presence of various translation-inhibiting antibiotics.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (1VY4 — Crystal Structure of Thermus thermophilus 70S Ribosome with A-, P-, and E-Site tRNAs)

node_peptidyl_transferase.title: The Peptidyl Transferase Center (PTC Ribozyme)
node_peptidyl_transferase.subtitle: Substrate-Assisted Catalysis in the 28S rRNA Domain V Core

metrics.catalytic_nature: Pure Ribozyme (Zero protein amino acid side chains within 18 Å of the active site)
metrics.rate_enhancement: Accelerates peptide bond formation >10^7 fold over uncatalyzed rate
metrics.mechanism_type: Substrate-assisted catalysis via pucker positioning and entropy reduction

mechanism: Located deep within Domain V of the 28S rRNA (large ribosomal subunit). Unlike classic protein enzymes that use catalytic amino acid residues (like His or Cys) in their active sites, the Peptidyl Transferase Center contains ZERO protein side chains within 18 angstroms of the reaction center.

Catalysis is driven by substrate-assisted geometry: the 28S rRNA structural RNA scaffold precisely positions the alpha-amino group of the A-site aminoacyl-tRNA and the ester carbonyl carbon of the P-site peptidyl-tRNA, lowering activation entropy and facilitating nucleophilic attack.
csir_high_yield: Definitive Proof of Ribozyme Catalysis: Thomas Cech and Harry Noller proved that highly deproteinized ribosomes (stripped of >95% of ribosomal proteins using SDS and phenol extraction) retain robust peptidyl transferase activity as long as the 23S/28S rRNA core remains intact!
Inhibitor Target: Chloramphenicol binds the PTC of bacterial ribosomes and blocks aminoacyl-tRNA binding, whereas Lincomycin and Clindamycin inhibit peptidyl transfer.
pathology: Chloramphenicol Toxicity: While specific to bacterial 70S ribosomes, high doses can inhibit human mitochondrial 55S mitoribosomes (which share bacterial ancestry), causing reversible bone marrow suppression and aplastic anemia.
lab_workbench: Fragment Reaction Assay (Monro & Lipmann): Testing whether ribosomes can catalyze the transfer of N-formylmethionine from an oligonucleotide donor (CCA-fMet) to puromycin in the absence of mRNA and template.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (1K9M — Noller Crystal Structure of Haloarcula marismortui 50S Subunit Domain V Peptidyl Transferase Center)

node_eef2_translocation.title: Elongation Factor Translocation (eEF2 & GTP Hydrolysis)
node_eef2_translocation.subtitle: Ratchet-like Subunit Rotation & tRNA Migration (A->P and P->E)

metrics.gtp_consumption: 2 GTP hydrolyzed per amino acid added (1 by eEF1A + 1 by eEF2)
metrics.conformational_shift: Small 40S subunit ratchets ~6° relative to the large 60S subunit

mechanism: After peptide bond formation, the newly lengthened peptidyl-tRNA resides in the hybrid A/P state (its CCA end is in the large subunit P-site, while its anticodon remains in the small subunit A-site).

Elongation factor eEF2-GTP binds the ribosome, and GTP hydrolysis drives a conformational ratchet-like rotation of the 40S subunit relative to the 60S subunit. This physical shift moves the tRNAs precisely one codon forward: A->P and P->E, resetting the A-site for the next incoming aminoacyl-tRNA.
csir_high_yield: Energy Accounting for Protein Synthesis (CSIR Part C Numerical):
• 1 ATP equivalent to aminoacylate tRNA (AMP attachment via aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase).
• 1 GTP hydrolyzed by eEF1A during aminoacyl-tRNA delivery to A-site.
• 1 GTP hydrolyzed by eEF2 during translocation.
Total energy cost = 4 high-energy phosphate bonds per peptide bond formed!
Inhibitor: Sordarin specifically targets eukaryotic eEF2, blocking translocation.
pathology: Pseudomonas Exotoxin A: Like Diphtheria toxin, it catalyzes the ADP-ribosylation of Diphtamide on elongation factor eEF2, shutting down host cell protein synthesis and causing tissue necrosis.
lab_workbench: Toe-Printing Assay (Primer Extension Inhibition): Reverse transcriptase stalls when it hits a ribosome halted by eEF2 inhibitors, revealing the exact nucleotide position of the ribosome on mRNA.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (4V5L — Cryo-EM Structure of Yeast Elongation Factor eEF2 Bound to the 80S Ribosome)

node_calnexin_cycle.title: The Calnexin / Calreticulin Lectin Folding Cycle
node_calnexin_cycle.subtitle: Glucosidase I/II & UGGT Quality Control Sensor for N-Linked Glycoproteins

metrics.glycan_tag: High-mannose core with terminal glucose residues (Glc3Man9GlcNAc2)

mechanism: As nascent glycoproteins enter the ER lumen, Glucosidases I and II trim the outer two glucose residues, leaving a monoglucosylated glycan (Glc1Man9GlcNAc2).

The membrane-bound lectin Calnexin (and soluble Calreticulin) binds this single glucose residue, holding the protein near ER protein disulfide isomerase (PDI) to assist proper disulfide bond formation.

Glucosidase II then removes the final glucose. If the protein is folded correctly, it exits the ER toward the Golgi. If it is still unfolded, the folding sensor enzyme **UGGT** (UDP-glucose:glycoprotein glucosyltransferase) recognizes exposed hydrophobic patches and adds a single glucose back onto the glycan, recycling it through the Calnexin cycle for another folding attempt!
csir_high_yield: UGGT as the Master Conformation Sensor (CSIR Part C): UGGT acts purely as a folding sensor—it ignores correctly folded proteins but recognizes molten globule / incompletely folded intermediates and re-glucosylates them so Calnexin can bind them again.
Castanospermine and Deoxynojirimycin are classic pharmacological inhibitors of Glucosidase I and II that disrupt the Calnexin cycle and cause premature protein aggregation.
pathology: Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency (Z Variant): A single Glu342Lys mutation causes alpha-1 antitrypsin to misfold in the ER. Retained in polymers by ER quality control, it causes neonatal hepatitis and early-onset emphysema due to uninhibited neutrophil elastase destruction of lung tissue.
lab_workbench: Concanavalin A (Con A) Lectin Affinity Chromatography: Isolates high-mannose ER glycoproteins from cell lysates to quantify folding intermediate proportions.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (1JHN — Crystal Structure of Mammalian Calreticulin P-Domain)

node_erad_degradation.title: ER-Associated Degradation (ERAD) & The 26S Proteasome
node_erad_degradation.subtitle: Retrotranslocation Out of the ER, Ubiquitination & Cytosolic Destruction

metrics.cytosolic_puller: p97 / VCP AAA+ ATPase (Extracts ubiquitinated chains into cytosol)

mechanism: When a protein fails folding quality control after repeated cycles, it is targeted for ER-Associated Degradation (ERAD).
STEP 1 (Retrotranslocation): The misfolded glycoprotein is threaded backward out of the ER lumen into the cytosol through a retrotranslocon channel (such as Sec61 or Derlin complexes).
STEP 2 (Ubiquitination): As it emerges into the cytosol, E3 ubiquitin ligases (e.g., Hrd1) attach multi-ubiquitin chains onto lysine residues.

STEP 3 (Proteasome Destruction): The cytosolic AAA+ ATPase chaperone p97/VCP extracts the ubiquitinated protein and delivers it to the 26S Proteasome, where it is unfolded and degraded into small peptides.
csir_high_yield: CFTR DeltaF508 Mutation (Classic CSIR Molecular Biology Example): Deletion of Phenylalanine 508 in Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Conductance Regulator (CFTR) causes a slight local folding defect. Although the mutant Cl- channel retains partial ion transport function, ERAD machinery recognizes it as misfolded, retrotranslocates it, and destroys it in the proteasome before it ever reaches the plasma membrane!

Proteasome Inhibitors: Bortezomib (Velcade) inhibits the 20S proteasome chymotrypsin-like site, causing toxic accumulation of misfolded proteins that triggers terminal UPR apoptosis in multiple myeloma plasma cells.
pathology: Cystic Fibrosis: The DeltaF508 ERAD degradation defect prevents chloride transport in lung epithelial cells, leading to thick, viscous mucus and chronic Pseudomonas bacterial infections.
lab_workbench: MG132 Proteasome Inhibition Assay: Treating cells with MG132 blocks the 26S proteasome, rescuing unstable ERAD substrates and allowing visualization of ubiquitinated intermediates by Western blot.

node_upr_sensors.title: The Unfolded Protein Response (UPR): IRE1, PERK & ATF6
node_upr_sensors.subtitle: Transmembrane Stress Sensors Restoring ER Proteostasis

metrics.sensor_1: IRE1 (Inositol-Requiring Enzyme 1) — Endonuclease that splices XBP1 mRNA
metrics.sensor_2: PERK (PKR-like ER Kinase) — Phosphorylates eIF2alpha to shut down translation
metrics.sensor_3: ATF6 (Activating Transcription Factor 6) — Migrates to Golgi for proteolytic release

mechanism: When unfolded proteins accumulate in the ER lumen faster than the folding/ERAD capacity, BiP (Hsp70 chaperone) dissociates from three transmembrane sensors, triggering the Unfolded Protein Response (UPR):

1. IRE1 PATHWAY: Dimerizes and autophosphorylates, activating an unconventional cytoplasmic endoribonuclease domain that splices XBP1 mRNA. Spliced XBP1s encodes a potent transcription factor driving genes for ER expansion and lipid synthesis.

2. PERK PATHWAY: Dimerizes and phosphorylates eIF2alpha on Serine-51. This globally halts general translation initiation (lowering ER load), while paradoxically allowing translation of stress-response genes like ATF4.

3. ATF6 PATHWAY: Translocates to the Golgi apparatus, where Site-1 and Site-2 proteases (S1P/S2P) cleave off its cytosolic domain, releasing an active transcription factor that upregulates chaperones (BiP/GRP78).
csir_high_yield: The eIF2alpha Paradox (CSIR Part C Favorite): Phosphorylation of eIF2alpha by PERK inhibits eIF2B (the guanine nucleotide exchange factor), preventing the recycling of eIF2-GDP to eIF2-GTP. This shuts down general protein synthesis across the cell, yet specific mRNAs with upstream open reading frames (like ATF4) are preferentially translated!
Fate Decision of UPR: If ER stress is mild, UPR restores homeostasis (adaptive UPR); if ER stress is prolonged and unresolvable, UPR activates CHOP (GADD153) and triggers apoptosis (terminal UPR).
pathology: Wolfram Syndrome: Mutations in WFS1 (encoding an ER membrane protein regulating ATF6 stability) cause childhood-onset diabetes mellitus, optic atrophy, and neurodegeneration due to unmitigated ER stress.
lab_workbench: RT-PCR with flanking primers across the XBP1 unconventional splice junction: Resolves the 26-nt intron excision by IRE1 on an agarose gel as a distinct molecular weight shift.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (3QE4 — Crystal Structure of Yeast IRE1 Luminal Domain in Complex with Unfolded Peptide)

agents.name: Cycloheximide
agents.mechanism_of_action: Binds E-site / PTC cleft of the 60S large ribosomal subunit
agents.rescue_experiment: Classic CSIR NET Tool: Completely freezes eukaryotic translation elongation by blocking peptidyl transferase activity and tRNA movement. Used in pulse-chase assays to instantly lock polysomes and nascent chains on mRNAs.

agents.name: Puromycin
agents.mechanism_of_action: Ribosomal A-site structural analog of aminoacyl-tRNA 3' end
agents.rescue_experiment: Enters the A-site, accepts the nascent polypeptide chain from the P-site, and causes premature chain termination, releasing truncated peptidyl-puromycin conjugates into the cytosol.

agents.name: Tunicamycin
agents.mechanism_of_action: Inhibits GlcNAc phosphotransferase (GPT / DPAGT1) on ER membrane

predicted_phenotype.upr_activation: Maximal (IRE1, PERK, and ATF6 fully triggered)

agents.rescue_experiment: Blocks the very first step of dolichol-linked oligosaccharide synthesis in the ER, preventing all N-linked glycosylation. Misfolded unglycosylated proteins flood the lumen, triggering massive UPR activation and ER stress.

agents.name: Bortezomib (Velcade)
agents.mechanism_of_action: Chymotrypsin-like catalytic site of the 20S core proteasome
agents.rescue_experiment: Prevents degradation of ERAD retrotranslocated substrates, causing toxic protein aggregates in the cytoplasm and terminal UPR apoptosis, highly effective against antibody-secreting multiple myeloma cells.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the targeting complex whose SRP54 subunit binds an N-terminal hydrophobic signal peptide and uses mutual GTP hydrolysis with its receptor to hand off to Sec61.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Correct! SRP binds the signal peptide and docks with the SRP receptor, utilizing GTP hydrolysis to transfer the ribosome to the Sec61 translocon.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the catalytic center inside the 60S ribosomal subunit whose active site contains zero protein amino acid side chains within 18 angstroms.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Spot on! The Peptidyl Transferase Center (PTC) in Domain V of 28S rRNA is a pure ribozyme that catalyzes peptide bond formation.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the quality control folding sensor enzyme that adds a single glucose back onto high-mannose glycans of incompletely folded glycoproteins to restart the Calnexin cycle.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Exact match! UGGT monitors glycoprotein folding status and reglucosylates misfolded intermediates for re-binding to Calnexin/Calreticulin.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the Upr transmembrane sensor that acts as an unconventional endoribonuclease to splice XBP1 mRNA during ER stress.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Correct! IRE1 dimerizes during ER stress and splices XBP1 mRNA to generate an active transcription factor promoting ER homeostasis.
